item.title: Barry Manilow cancels concert 45 minutes before start amid ongoing lung cancer recovery
item.description: Barry Manilow canceled his Lexington show just 45 minutes before showtime, citing unforeseen circumstances amid his ongoing lung cancer battle.
item.content:encoded:
Barry Manilow canceled his Kentucky show on Tuesday just 45 minutes before it was scheduled to start.

"Due to unforeseen circumstances tonight’s show in Lexington has been rescheduled," Manilow, who was diagnosed with lung cancer last year, wrote on X ahead of the concert. No other explanation was given.

While some slammed Manilow as "disrespectful" for the late cancellation, others were quick to offer him words of encouragement.

BARRY MANILOW, 82, GIVES UPDATE ON HIS CANCER BATTLE AS HE CANCELS MORE TOUR DATES

"Sending hugs x take care and remember you must come first," one user wrote on X.

"I'm so sorry you've had to reschedule tonight's show," another added. "Please look after yourself Barry, sending much love and healing energy from across the pond."

In December, Manilow revealed he had been diagnosed with early-stage lung cancer after doctors discovered a cancerous spot on his left lung following a bout of bronchitis.

"As many of you know I recently went through six weeks of bronchitis followed by a relapse of another five weeks," Manilow wrote on Instagram at the time. "Even though I was over the bronchitis and back on stage at the Westgate Las Vegas, my wonderful doctor ordered an MRI just to make sure that everything was OK. The MRI discovered a cancerous spot on my left lung that needs to be removed. It's pure luck (and a great doctor) that it was found so early. That's the good news."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"The bad news is that now that the Christmas A Gift of Love concerts are over I'm going into surgery to have the spot removed," he continued. "The doctors do not believe it has spread and I'm taking tests to confirm the diagnosis. So, that's it. No chemo. No radiation. Just chicken soup and I Love Lucy reruns."

In February, Manilow announced he was rescheduling additional February and March dates on the tour after a "very depressing visit" with his surgeon.

That same month, the "Copacabana" singer detailed a tough conversation he had with his doctor.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"He said, ‘Barry, you won’t be ready to do a 90-minute show. Your lungs aren’t ready yet,’" Manilow continued.

"You’re in great shape considering what you’ve been through, but your body isn’t ready. You shouldn’t do the first arena shows. You won’t make it through."

Manilow continued, "I had a feeling he’d say that. Deep down… my body knew what my heart didn’t want to admit: I wasn’t ready... When I do come back, I will COME BACK!!!"

In May, Manilow announced that while he had to cancel his "Hits Come Home" residency dates that month at Westgate Resort in Las Vegas, he's "making great progress" with his lung cancer treatment and plans to return to the stage sooner rather than later.

"Good news! I went to the doctor yesterday and he said I’m making great progress and look great! Well of course I do! Thank you very much!" he wrote on X. "All the training and exercising I’ve put in is paying off."

"He did say, however, that I’m not quite ready for Vegas. That means I won’t be able to return for our May shows at @WestgateVegas. But the good news is he said I will be ready for my June arena shows in the UK. It’s going to be great to see you all in the UK. Westgate Las Vegas is my home away from home… and I’ll see you all in July. In the meantime… come to the UK! We’ll be there in June and hope you will be too! See you then… Barry."

Fox News Digital's Ashley Hume contributed to this post.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Experts crowned El-Sayed — then Michigan voters turned his win into a near-disaster
item.description: Polls gave Abdul El-Sayed double-digit leads, but Haley Stevens nearly pulled off a stunning upset in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary race.
item.content:encoded:
Over the past week, prior to far-left candidate Abdul El-Sayed squeaking to a possible victory over Rep. Haley Stevens in Tuesday’s Democratic Senate primary, the contest was treated by almost everyone in the news media as over, with El-Sayed a shoo-in.

I had been in Michigan reporting on the race, and what I wrote was the exact opposite: It was clear to me the race was tightening, especially after the endorsement of Gov. Gretchen Whitmer. So when I saw every subsequent poll giving El-Sayed double-digit leads, I was shocked and a bit nervous.

Maybe, for the first time, the ground had lied to me and the numbers guys had this one right. But once again, the ground coverage defeated the aerial polling.

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

But by Wednesday morning, this race, in which El-Sayed held a 95% to 5% advantage in prediction markets, had not been called, with El-Sayed seeming to head toward a meager 1- to 3-point victory, with his total under 50%.

Notably, Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who dropped out of the race, still netted 4% — or, put another way, the difference.

As for the polling, the last five public polls had El-Sayed winning by 19, 17, 14, 16 and 11 points, respectively. The news media took this as gospel, and instead of covering a surging Stevens with a real chance to win — as I did — they covered an El-Sayed coronation pre-party.

What surprised me so much about this polling was that in Detroit, after dozens of interviews, I couldn’t find anyone voting for El-Sayed who wasn’t already an activist in some way. The more ordinary the politics or occupation of the voter, the more likely that person was to support Stevens.

DAVID MARCUS: IN BOOMING DETROIT, VOTERS SKEPTICAL OF SOCIALISM SNAKE OIL

As I put it in these pages then, "Many Democratic voters I talked to wanted a steadier hand on the system, and they want to beat Trump and the GOP. But they don’t want to blow up the system."

Those voters, whom I met in Detroit diners and bars, were invisible to the pollsters. Yet, in the end, between Stevens and McMorrow, they were the majority of Democratic voters.

There needs to be a serious reckoning over how journalists use polls and prediction markets in the wake of this historic polling miss, because there is every reason to believe Stevens could have won if her very real momentum had been accurately described.

Elections are stories, and they have arcs. The last week of this campaign, by all rights, should have been about "The Stevens Comeback," but instead, the polls told the story: "El-Sayed Blowout."

DSA MEMBER LEADS DEM PRIMARY IN MIDWEST BATTLEGROUND BUT TRAILS LIKELY GOP NOMINEE: POLL

How many potential Stevens voters stayed home on Tuesday as a result? We will never know.

The national coverage throughout the week leading to Election Day was that even with Whitmer’s endorsement and that of Rep. James Clyburn, D-S.C., to shore up the Black vote, El-Sayed and his communist-aligned podcaster ally, Hasan Piker, were cruising to victory.

Let’s be honest: It is the story everybody wanted. It is the sexy story of young socialists upending the Democratic Party establishment, but the embellished polls may well have become a self-fulfilling prophecy.

For Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers, this is all excellent news. He wanted to run against the socialist-aligned El-Sayed, and now he will. He also has the advantage of El-Sayed’s being wounded by what turned into a humiliating underperformance.

EL-SAYED PALS AROUND WITH FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER THE DAY BEFORE CRUCIAL MICHIGAN SENATE ELECTION

Rogers should also be buoyed by El-Sayed surrogate Piker’s statement Tuesday night about possibly reaching out to Stevens voters. Piker said: saying, "Everyone being like, 'Abdul has a f--- ton of work to do mending bridges' … You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of sh---. You literally called the dude a f---ing terrorist for months on end …  And now you're going to say sit there and be like, 'you really gotta come to me now.'"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

These are not the sweet, sonorous sounds of intraparty unity.

The race between Rogers and El-Sayed will be close and hard-fought, and I will find my way back to the Great Lakes State to take the temperature. In the meantime, the news media must be much more skeptical of polling because it may have turned this primary.

item.title: Cleveland's new WNBA team rejects 'Lady Cavaliers' identity in unveiling of name, color scheme
item.description: Cleveland's new WNBA expansion team unveiled its name, logo and two shades of blue — rejecting the Cavaliers' wine and gold for a Lake Erie identity.
item.content:encoded:
Sirens: mythical creatures who perched along rocky shores, using their beautiful, hypnotic songs to lure unsuspecting sailors to their deaths.

Also, Cleveland’s new WNBA team.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The expansion franchise unveiled its name, logo and colors Tuesday, officially introducing the Cleveland Sirens ahead of the team’s inaugural season in 2028.

The nautical branding is a nod to Lake Erie, but the organization had another objective in mind: making sure the new team did not look like a women’s version of the Cleveland Cavaliers.

"We don't want to be the Lady Cavaliers, and we don't want to be wine and gold," Sirens President of Business Operations Allison Howard said. "We really need to be very separate, very distinctive."

The Sirens and Cavaliers are both owned by Dan Gilbert’s Rock Entertainment Group and will share Rocket Arena. But Cleveland’s WNBA leadership made clear from the beginning that the two franchises should not share an identity.

Instead of borrowing the Cavaliers’ color scheme, the Sirens will use two shades of blue — appropriately named "Sirens Blue" and "Erie Blue." Their logo features the mythical creature beneath the team name, while the "S" in the wordmark contains a hidden "CLE."

"We love our Cavaliers, and they are such an amazing part of this organization," Howard said. "But this team can exist very much on the independent side of the Cavaliers."

Howard said the organization expects the Sirens to attract a different audience than the Cavaliers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"They eat different food, they drink different drinks," Howard said. "They get here earlier. They purchase merchandise differently, and they come from all over the state and even outside the state."

WNBA SILENT AFTER CAITLIN CLARK SAYS LEAGUES SHOULD DETERMINE WHO SHOULD BE INCLUDED IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Cleveland’s approach differs from several WNBA teams that share ownership with NBA counterparts. The Los Angeles Sparks mirror the Lakers’ purple and gold, while the Phoenix Mercury use the Suns’ purple and orange. The Minnesota Lynx and Timberwolves also feature similar combinations of blue and green, and the Indiana Fever share navy and gold with the Pacers, though the Fever incorporate red into their identity, too.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

The Sirens, however, are taking a path closer to the New York Liberty and Golden State Valkyries, which both separate themselves visually from their city’s NBA franchises.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

The Sirens will not be Cleveland’s first WNBA team.

The Cleveland Rockers were one of the league’s original eight franchises when the WNBA launched in 1997. Named as a tribute to the city’s Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, the Rockers played seven seasons before folding in 2003 after owner Gordon Gund was unable to find a buyer.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Former Rockers player Janice Braxton narrated the Sirens’ introductory video, which carried the theme "Hear the Call." Braxton and several other former Rockers players also attended Tuesday’s unveiling.

The new franchise has already collected approximately 9,000 season-ticket deposits, and Howard expects that number to grow now that Cleveland fans finally know the name of their team.

item.title: Controversial socialist chef flip-flops on abolish the police, says she’s ‘serious about public safety’
item.description: Francesca Hong now says she is "serious about public safety" after previously calling to defund and abolish the police in her 2020 tweets.
item.content:encoded:
Controversial chef and democratic socialist candidate Francesca Hong has reversed her position on defunding and abolishing the police, saying in a recent podcast interview that she has become "serious about public safety."

Hong is a Wisconsin Democratic lawmaker perhaps best known for her 2020 call to "cancel Thanksgiving" because of its colonial history. She is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and a leading Democratic candidate for Wisconsin governor.

In an episode of "Pod Save America" released on Tuesday, Hong was asked about her 2020 tweets in which she wrote that "police exist to uphold white supremacy" and "I support defunding the police as a first step towards abolishing the police." The podcast host asked her, "I’m wondering how your views on policing have evolved since 2020?"

In response, Hong said, "My views have only become stronger in that I’m serious about public safety and I will not abolish the police."

SOCIALIST FRANCESCA HONG STRUGGLES TO EXPLAIN CALL TO 'CANCEL THANKSGIVING' AS POST RESURFACES

"My views are that people are struggling right now and need basic needs met, and I want to focus on stopping violent crime and giving law enforcement the resources and the training that they need, but ensure we are also holding accountable law enforcement that does not follow the law," she added.

Pressed on whether she still believes police exist to uphold White supremacy, Hong answered quickly, "No."

Hong was then asked, "What has changed in your thinking since you posted that in 2020?"

She answered, "I’ve had more conversations with people who are more directly connected to the problems and have learned that it is most important for a public servant like myself to make sure we’re looking at sensible, practical solutions that will help keep communities safe."

LEFT’S LATEST SOCIALIST DARLING DRAGGED OVER ‘WHITENESS’ COMMENTS PULLING IN HER OWN FAMILY: ‘WEIRDO RACISM’

"When you talk to people who are most justice impacted, a mother who lost a child to police violence, people who have contended with injustices in historically marginalized communities, but just also looks like making sure we are implementing solutions and helping change the material conditions of people’s lives," she said.

During the interview, Hong also characterized her previous statement fantasizing about a "world without prisons" as "more aspirational."

Critics have argued that Hong has a history of expressing controversial progressive takes, with former X posts resurfacing in recent weeks.

In 2019, she wrote, "I ate two bites of my kid’s cheeseburger at a Culver’s in black river falls and told him they ran out of ice cream. Mostly just wanted to leave bc I was on the verge of a [sic] anxiety attack… to [sic] many old white people who didn’t think we spoke English."

DEMOCRATS' SHARP LEFT TURN? DSA'S INFLUENCE GROWS AS MIDTERMS, 2028 RACES TAKES SHAPE

In another since-deleted post, Hong wrote, "Cancel Thanksgiving. Should have done this in 1621. If it takes a worldwide pandemic for us to realize we should stop celebrating colonialism and the original superspreader event that killed indigenous folx [sic] and women, so be it."

In a recent CNN appearance, Hong was asked, "Do you still believe that Thanksgiving should be canceled?"

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"I’m a chef, and one of the first meals that I made that was for the community when I was 16 [years old] was a Thanksgiving meal," Hong responded. "But Thanksgiving is also a time that’s incredibly painful for many people in our communities. And so, I think there, I wanted to make sure that people understood that there are multiple views, but views can evolve."

Fox News Digital reached out to Hong, Pod Save America and the DSA for additional comment.

item.title: Puka Nacua, due for new contract, hires Zay Flowers' agency after Ravens star's massive $140 million deal
item.description: Puka Nacua hired Zay Flowers' agent after the Ravens star's $140 million extension, positioning himself to potentially top the highest-paid receiver.
item.content:encoded:
Puka Nacua is taking notes.

The Los Angeles Rams wide receiver is beginning his fourth NFL season next month, making him due for quite a payday.

Nacua's 95.3 receiving yards per game are the most all-time, and since joining the league in 2023, no one else within six yards of him.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Once an afterthought as a fifth-round selection, Nacua is now in the conversation as the best wide receiver in the league, and he wants to be paid like it.

Well, after Zay Flowers inked a $140 million extension that gives him $108 million guaranteed, both figures are the fourth-highest ever at the position, Nacua has reportedly brought in Flowers' agent to negotiate his next contract.

Like Flowers, Nacua is now represented by WIN Sports Group after previously being a part of the Athletes First team. WIN also represents stars like Dexter Lawrence, Jordan Davis, Nnamdi Madubuike, and Dion Dawkins.

Because Nacua wasn't drafted in the first round, unlike Flowers, he is not eligible for a fifth-year option, making him set to hit free agency upon the 2026 season's end.

ANTHONY FAUCI’S LAWYER SAYS AARON RODGERS 'SHOULD STICK TO FOOTBALL ’ AFTER SCORCHING HIM ON PAT MCAFEE'S SHOW

Flowers and Nacua entered the league the same year, and given that Nacua's numbers are better than Flowers' across the board, the Rams star figures to have a good argument to not only beat Flowers' deal but maybe even surpass Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the highest-paid receiver of all time ($168.6 million).

Despite Flowers playing in 50 games compared with Nacua's 44, Flowers has more than 1,000 fewer receiving yards and 76 fewer receptions.

Flowers has undoubtedly been a stalwart for the Baltimore Ravens, as he's coming off a season in which he caught 86 passes for 1,211 yards and five touchdowns. He’s now posted back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons. Yet had Nacua not missed six games because of injury in 2024, he may very well already have more than 4,500 yards (he had more than 90 receiving yards per game that season).

Flowers has missed only one regular-season game in three seasons (his rookie campaign), although he was unavailable for the 2024 playoffs.

He became the fastest player in Ravens history (21 games) to reach 100 receptions and the first Raven with multiple 1,000-yard seasons in the first three years of his career. He ranked 11th in the NFL in receptions in 2025 and seventh in receiving yards. That was despite an underwhelming, injury-plagued season from Jackson — and Baltimore's willingness to run the ball with Derrick Henry.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: White House pushes 'watershed' fraud-fighting reform in Congress as Vance convenes task force
item.description: Vice President JD Vance participated in an anti-fraud task force roundtable event on Wednesday, proposing reforms to help crackdown on fraud.
item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance, who chairs President Donald Trump's Task Force To Eliminate Fraud, said during remarks on Wednesday that the effort has identified $230 billion of suspected fraud so far.

"We've been able to stop $56 billion in fraudulent payments that would've otherwise gone to fraudsters, rather than to the people who need them," he said at a task-force roundtable event with lawmakers.

Vance called for reforms to help tackle the fraud.

VANCE TO HOST CONGRESS AT WHITE HOUSE TO DISCUSS LEGISLATIVE ACTION ON FRAUD

He said when the federal government distributes money to states for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), the federal government has "no visibility into who is ultimately getting those benefits."

He said that if California provides "those food stamp benefits to an illegal alien, to a violent criminal, the federal government has no visibility, and sometimes the states themselves have no visibility."

"So we need to work with Congress, and we need some legislation that would actually force some data sharing between the state governments and the federal governments," the vice president said.

TOP FEDERAL PROSECUTOR CALLS CALIFORNIA A 'FRAUDSTER'S PARADISE,' WARNS STATE OFFICIALS COULD FACE CHARGES

Vance also floated the idea of tougher sentencing against those convicted of fraud.

White House deputy chief of staff for policy and Homeland Security advisor Stephen Miller called for "strict, clear, mandatory minimums" for fraudsters, saying they should be slapped with "a very substantial prison sentence."

DOJ CHARGES 19 DEFENDANTS IN ALLEGED $4M PHILADELPHIA MEDICARE AND MEDICAID FRAUD

"That change alone would be watershed for fighting fraud because it would mean that the Department of Justice would be able to, through prosecuting a few hundred or thousand cases in a year, be able to chill the criminal conduct of millions," Miller said.

item.title: LIV Golf CEO quiets speculation with announcement of new investor to keep circuit afloat into 2027
item.description: Scott O'Neil says a lead investor has been secured to keep LIV Golf alive beyond 2026, with players set to become majority equity holders in the league.
item.content:encoded:
Long live LIV?

The Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced in April that it would stop funding LIV Golf following the 2026 season. With the sole funder of the breakaway circuit cutting off the money spigot, it was speculated that LIV, or at least the current version of it, would cease to exist beyond this year.

On Wednesday, LIV CEO Scott O'Neil halted that speculation.

Speaking ahead of this week's LIV New York tournament at Trump National Bedminster, O'Neil announced that an investor has been secured to keep the circuit afloat. While O'Neil did not divulge any specific details about the unknown investor, he did share an incredibly important fact about the next phase of LIV Golf and its players.

"LIV Golf has an agreement in place with a lead investor, signed by the investor and approved by the Board, to anchor the transaction and play a key role in supporting the path forward for the League’s next era, driven by and for the players," O'Neil said.

"Notably, our next chapter will make our players the majority equity holders in LIV Golf, a first for a major global sports league," he continued, while stating the goal is to enter a finalized transaction in September.

Aside from players holding a majority of the equity, it is unclear what LIV Golf looks like, and even more unclear which players will be competing, beginning in 2027. The plan for the 2027 LIV schedule is for it to feature 10 events, with five in the United States and five across the globe.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The announcement that LIV will be around beyond 2026 comes as the unknowns still continue to add up regarding whether or not the LIV Team Championship, set for Aug. 27-30, will even be contested. The update on 2027 investments does not appear to have any bearing on the Team Championship.

It was reported at the end of July that the season finale is expected to be canceled after "multiple contractors" told Flushing It Golf that their travel and accommodations have been canceled and that "money is also owed."

LIV golfer and former major champion Martin Kaymer went on the record with Today's Golfer that the team championship was "highly unlikely" to take place.

A source with knowledge of the ongoing situation shared with OutKick on July 29 that LIV was continuing to have positive discussions with prospective investors for LIV Golf 2.0 while working to secure funding for the circuit's future and long-term sustainability.

Based on the league's announcement on Wednesday, the discussions with prospective investors were, in fact, positive.

item.title: Government-run grocery stores face renewed scrutiny after Chicago's experiment fizzles
item.description: Chicago spent $13.5 million on government-run grocery stores now on the brink of collapse after Save A Lot terminated its Yellow Banana agreement.
item.content:encoded:
The idea of government-run grocery stores is facing renewed scrutiny as Chicago abandons plans for a municipal supermarket, raising questions about whether taxpayer-funded markets can survive.

"Chicago's city-run grocery stores are on the brink of collapse after a Save A Lot terminated its licensing agreement with stores operated by Yellow Banana," Bryce Hill, director of fiscal and economic analysis at Illinois Policy, told Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

"So the city spent $13.5 million on these stores, but now they're on the brink of closing. They were meant to address food security and availability in what the city deems food desks, but this outcome should really come as no surprise," Hill said.

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

Rob Karr, president and CEO of the Illinois Retail Merchants Association, told Fox News Digital Monday that the experiment is failing in multiple areas.

"So what we're seeing, particularly in New York and Seattle, are proposals to having the government actually artificially lowering prices by using their general revenue funds to make those groceries ‘more affordable,’ The state looked at that here in Illinois and dismissed it because it's inherently flawed," Karr said. "It has failed everywhere it has worked because it doesn't recognize the realities of the marketplace."

Chicago officials ultimately shifted away from opening a city-owned grocery store, opting instead to support privately operated neighborhood markets.

The Center Square reported Sunday that the closure of seven Save A Lot stores on Chicago's South and West sides has reignited questions about whether taxpayer-funded grocery initiatives can improve food access in low-income communities.

SNAP FOOD STAMP FRAUD HAS NEFARIOUS TERRORISM LINKS, TOP AGRICULTURE WATCHDOG WARNS CONGRESS

In the article, Nicole Huyer, a free-market policy analyst, said the closures underscore the shortcomings of government-backed solutions.

The outlet also reported that the stores, managed by retail platform Yellow Banana, closed after Save A Lot terminated its operating agreement with the company, pointing to financial challenges that included a significant decrease in SNAP purchases.

The Whole Foods in Chicago’s Englewood neighborhood, which closed in 2022, received a significant government subsidy, relying on an $11 million Tax Increment Financing (TIF) subsidy from the City of Chicago.

When it closed, local outlet WTTW reported that state Rep. Sonya Harper, D-Chicago, said in a statement that she was disappointed in the development, as the store had said it was not about making a profit but about ensuring access to healthy food.

"I was proud to work with Whole Foods to bring a new location to Englewood because they claimed their decision was not based on profitability, but rather a desire to help provide access to healthy groceries for residents," Harper said in the statement.

STEVE FORBES: 4 WAYS TO FIX WHAT’S WRONG WITH NEW YORK CITY AND STOP THE EXODUS

Hill told Fox News Digital that the areas where government grocery stores are failing tend to not be friendly to business.

"Illinois and Chicago specifically is one of the toughest places to do business. So, Illinois has the second-highest property taxes in the nation," Hill said. "They're even higher in Chicago. Commercial property here is taxed at 250% more than residential property, which makes it tougher for businesses to operate."

"So, property taxes are out of control, which affect business margins as well," Hill added. "But on top of that, for consumers and for businesses, Chicago's total sales tax, which also applies to groceries, was just at an increase on Aug. 1. So the total sales rate in the city is now 10.5%. It's the second highest of any city in the nation. If the city's serious about helping businesses and residents in need, it should start there rather than wasting millions of dollars on projects that we know are going to fail."

Karr told Fox News Digital that cities should look at practical ways to make it easier for grocery stores to operate.

CHICAGO POL SAYS WALGREENS SHOULD BE CHARGED WITH 'FIRST-DEGREE CORPORATE ABANDONMENT' OVER CLOSURE OVER THEFT

"Instead of trying to use gimmicks, look at the real reasons why grocery stores are having a hard time staying open," Karr said.

"And frankly, the same applies to pharmacies," he added. "Although it's a little different because there's also pharmacy reimbursement at stake there. But when you look at grocery stores, what are your permitting processes? What are your licensing processes? What are your labor mandates? What's going on in your property tax? When you look at the city of Chicago and Cook County, we have the classification system where commercial and industrial carry two-thirds of the burden. That's a problem. You can't continue to pile those on and expect something to change."

Fox News Digital reached out to Yellow Banana and Whole Foods for comment.

item.title: Anthony Fauci’s lawyer says Aaron Rodgers 'should stick to football’ after scorching him on Pat McAfee's show
item.description: Aaron Rodgers called Anthony Fauci an "absolute coward" for pleading the Fifth 111 times, and Fauci's attorney fired back with a pointed response.
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Fauci may have taken the Fifth in the nation's capital, but his legal team isn't afraid to keep swinging.

Days after Fauci pleaded the Fifth 111 times during a Senate hearing on the advice of his attorneys, Aaron Rodgers could not help but rip the "absolute coward."

"Are you kidding me? You get a pardon, and you’re and you pleaded over 100 times at the White House? What are you scared of, Tony? I thought you were the science. ‘I am science,’ and you get up there and can’t answer a question? What are we doing?" Rodgers said on "The Pat McAfee Show" earlier this week.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Well, David Schertler, Fauci’s attorney, was asked by The Athletic to respond to Rodgers' criticism, and he did not hold back.

"Aaron Rodgers doesn’t know what he’s talking about. He should stick to football," Schertler said to the outlet.

Fauci was questioned by the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, chaired by Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., over his response to the pandemic and his policy decisions, during which the former White House COVID advisor was accused of funding gain-of-function research in Wuhan, China.

JERRY JONES 'OPEN' TO CO-OWNING COWBOYS WITH MARK CUBAN: 'ALL THE RESPECT IN THE WORLD FOR HIM'

"Spending the entire time writing in his diary about how fun it is to be famous. You gotta be kidding me. What are you going to say about me now? Seriously, what are they going to say about me now? Now, you can’t talk about the COVID stuff because obviously it was made in a lab in China," Rodgers continued.

"That’s like not even questionable anymore. Tony Fauci is an absolute criminal. It’s been a great life and a great career, and it’s nice to be sitting on this side now, especially after that coward pled the Fifth over 100 times. I thought you had a pardon there, Tony. Why couldn’t you answer one question the entire time?"

The Steelers, though, did not seem to be bothered much by what Rodgers said.

"Discussions around culture and politics can bring differing perspectives, and our players are entitled to their own personal views. With respect to that, I am certain there are a variety of opinions on many topics within our locker room," Steelers spokesman Burt Lauten said in a statement to Fox News Digital/OutKick.

Fauci’s refusal to answer has Rodgers going full tilt years after dealing with constant scrutiny, whether it’s the man himself or the network he has issues with. Rodgers drummed up controversy when he said he was "immunized" from COVID-19.

This season marks 22 years Rodgers has starred in the NFL, and he doubled down recently, saying this will be his final year.

Fox News' Scott Thompson and OutKick's Armando Salguero contributed to this report.

item.title: Two brothers deliver storybook moment by homering in respective debuts on same day in incredible fashion
item.description: George Lombard Jr. hit a home run in his Yankees debut while brother Jacob went deep in his pro debut with the Marlins on the same unforgettable day.

Aug. 4, 2026 is a day the Lombard family will remember for a long time.

Not one, but two brothers made their pro baseball debuts. George Lombard Jr. made his major league debut with the New York Yankees, while his younger brother, Jacob, made his professional debut in Low-A with the Miami Marlins organization.

Both brothers made debuts to remember, as they each blasted a home run with their new clubs.

George Lombard Sr. and his wife, Judy, had flights booked to watch their youngest son, Jacob, make his pro debut in Jupiter. However, upon hearing news of Lombard Jr.’s promotion, Jacob insisted the family should see his older brother in the Bronx instead.

"We found out about 11:30 p.m. last night, so pretty late last night. And my mom was preparing, getting ready to drive up here to Jupiter. It's not too far of a drive from Miami, but my brother calls my dad, my mom and I on the FaceTime, like we kind of do every night, and he tells us the news and we were kind of all jaw-dropped," Jacob Lombard said during an appearance on ESPN’s "SportsCenter."

"My mom was freaking out. My dad is on the other side of the country in Seattle. I told my mom, ‘Don't even think about it. You're not coming over here to Jupiter. You're going to New York. All you guys are going to New York.’ I'm very happy that the whole family got to go out there and see him and they got to watch kind of my game play out."

George Lombard Sr. played in the major leagues for six seasons and is currently the Detroit Tigers bench coach. The team allowed him to leave and attend his son’s debut in person.

Jacob Lombard hit his home run first. In the top of the third inning, Lombard, in his second at-bat, pummeled a breaking ball into the visitors' bullpen for a solo home run for the Jupiter Hammerheads.

EXCLUSIVE: ISRAELI PRESIDENT HERZOG BLASTS MAMDANI, PRAISES TRUMP, SOUNDS ALARM ON IRAN

Herzog's warning comes as newly released New York City Police Department (NYPD) data show anti-Jewish incidents accounted for 56.9% of all confirmed hate crimes since the start of 2026, even though Jewish New Yorkers make up only about 10% of the city's population.

Herzog pointed to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whom he accused of spreading hate and compromising the lives of New Yorkers.

"Mamdani does not respect my nation's right for self-determination — the Jewish people's inherent right to have a nation of their own. And he's basically spreading blasphemy, hate, antisemitic rhetoric. He should understand that he's risking his own citizens, he’s risking their safety, well-being and life," Herzog told Fox News Digital.

The J7 comprises Jewish communities in the United States, Australia, Canada, Argentina, the United Kingdom, Germany and France.

item.title: DARLINE GRAHAM: I'm South Carolina's newest senator. This is who I am and what I believe

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

For the past seven years, I led a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable and necessary. I fought against duplication of services knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars.

But beyond the resume, people want to know who I am and what I believe.

I'm a mother, a grandmother and a wife. I know how to bargain shop and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I'm a volleyball mom who loves nothing more than watching my daughter play, and I believe boys have no place in girls' sports and no business in girls' locker rooms.

I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions.

I stand for the national anthem.

I believe our veterans are heroes.

I will always Back the Blue.

I'm Darline Graham: a bargain shopper and a hard worker who knows your struggles because I live them too.

I'm not an expert on Congress — I am an expert on the problems facing families in South Carolina.

item.title: How 'Sopranos' star Vincent Pastore helped create the single greatest television season of all time
item.description: Vincent Pastore's Big Pussy drove the finest season of television ever made, from FBI informant reveals to fever dreams and a final boat ride.
item.content:encoded:
Fans of the "Sopranos" are still reeling from the loss of beloved star Vincent Pastore over the weekend.

The veteran actor known for playing Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero on the HBO crime drama was found dead in his Bronx home, and although he was only on the show for two seasons, his passing left a giant hole in the "Sopranos" community.

You can count me in as one of those fans who was particularly bummed to lose Pastore, because he contributed to what is perhaps the finest season of television that has ever been gifted to mankind.

RANKING THE MAJOR ANTAGONISTS OF 'THE SOPRANOS'

It's no secret that I love "The Sopranos," as a quick scroll through some of my work will yield a smattering of articles pontificating on every aspect of the show.

It's one of my favorite series of all time, and season two in particular represents what is, in my humble opinion, the apex of episodic television.

This is thanks in large part to Pastore's contributions as Tony Soprano's best friend and loyal soldier, Big Pussy.

Throughout most of season one, we are shown that Puss is Tony's confidant, even more so than his second-in-command, Silvio Dante.

Tony goes to Puss for advice about his son, among other things, showing the two have a connection that goes far beyond "the business."

But by the end of the first season, Puss is suspected to be an informant for the FBI, and before anyone from the Soprano crew can confirm their suspicions, he takes off for parts unknown, only setting off more alarm bells for Tony and company.

When he returns at the beginning of season two with an airtight alibi — going to Puerto Rico for acupuncture therapy to treat his ailing back — he has to re-earn the trust of his fellow crew members.

What makes Pussy's return unique, however, is that it is revealed early in the second season to the audience only that he's actually a rat, and the rest of the season is spent watching Tony subconsciously piecing together the evidence that his best friend is working with the feds to take him down.

It makes for riveting television the entire season, as we get several moments of tension as viewers know that Pussy has turned state's witness and could get whacked at any time.

Pussy's heel turn also gives us more insight into the FBI's inner workings, as the Bureau starts to become more of a main character thanks to the show focusing on his forced partnership with them.

This all culminates in the moment Tony finally figures it out, and the methods through which he arrives at the conclusion that his soldier is playing for the other team are some of the most creative and twisted in all of television.

In the penultimate episode of season two, Tony's biggest competition, Richie Aprile, gets taken out by his fiancée (Tony's sister Janice).

This happens right as Richie is about to make a move on Tony to take him out, so with one episode to wrap up the season, it appears as if all of Tony's worries are behind him.

Then we are reminded of the elephant — or in this case, rat — in the room.

After a late night meal at an Indian restaurant followed by a nightcap at the crew's favorite Italian restaurant, a season's worth of suspicions comes bubbling up for Tony in the form of a violent episode of food poisoning.

While deep in the throes of his intestinal Hell, Tony has a series of fever dreams that start out as subtle warnings and end up practically spelling it out for him.

"You know I've been working for the feds, right Ton'," a fish with Pussy's voice says to Tony.

It's so unique and brilliant, and I have no idea how the writers even came up with something like that, but it's easily my favorite hour of television ever made.

‘SOPRANOS’ STAR LORRAINE BRACCO SAYS SHE'S LOOKING FOR LOVE IN HER 70S

After that revelation, Tony and his crew take Pussy on a final, ill-fated boat ride where the compromised mobster cops to his crimes against the family before reminiscing on old times and sharing a final drink as Tony, Silvio, and Paulie draw their guns.

"You were like a brother to me. To all of us."

Before they have a chance to change their minds, the three heartbroken crew members unload their weapons into Pussy's chest and give him a burial at sea.

The episode and season end with a montage of all the destruction Tony and his crew have caused throughout the 13-episode run, interspersed with the mob boss enjoying the "fruits of his labor" at his daughter Meadow's high school graduation, blissfully unaware of (or unaffected by) the pain he's inflicted on his community.

The final shot lingers on the crashing waves of the North Jersey shoreline, reminding us of Pussy's ultimate fate, as the show fades to black while the haunting tones of The Rolling Stones' "Thru and Thru" play in the background.

It's perfect.

A perfect ending to a nearly perfect season of television.

And it's not just the Big Pussy storyline that makes season two must-watch TV, either.

The aforementioned Richie Aprile, played wonderfully by David Proval, makes for one of the most menacing villains of the series.

His back-and-forth with Tony throughout the season is equal parts hysterical and frightening, and he represents one of our protagonist's most formidable foes.

Season two also introduces another fan favorite to the cast in Furio Giunta, the native Italian who acts as Tony's enforcer and causes plenty of consternation between he and Pussy, as the latter (correctly) believes he is being replaced by the former.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

And I would be remiss if I didn't mention Tony's mother, Livia, who proves to be a bigger thorn in his side than even Richie at times throughout the show's run.

Nancy Marchand's turn as the morose, sociopathic matriarch of the Soprano family deserves special mention, particularly because she turned in such a masterful performance while battling the very cancer that would ultimately cost the actress her life shortly after season two wrapped.

"The Sopranos" would experience more highs throughout its six-ish season run, but none ever reached the zenith that was season two, in my opinion.

The writers are firing on all cylinders, the cast of characters is robust, and the plot lines are engaging enough to leave you begging for more at the end of each episode.

And none of it would have had the cultural impact it did if not for everyone's favorite FBI rat.

The world lost a legend in Vincent Pastore this past weekend, but his legacy lives on in perpetuity thanks to his turn as Salvatore Bonpensiero.

item.title: Brandt Snedeker is right to shut down the outside demand for younger Presidents Cup picks
item.description: Brandt Snedeker played a practice round with Jackson Koivun but says he won't pick young players for the Presidents Cup just for the sake of youth.
item.content:encoded:
There are bad problems, and there are good problems, and Brandt Snedeker has a whole bunch of the latter.

In less than 50 days, the 2026 Presidents Cup will get underway at Medinah Country Club, where the U.S. team will look to defeat the Internationals for the 11th straight time. Snedeker, the captain of the U.S. side, will have six of his 12 players selected for him via automatic qualifying, and then comes the inevitable difficult decisions surrounding his six captain's picks to round out his team.

With the Presidents Cup being both entirely lopsided and a gargantuan rung below the Ryder Cup on the ladder of significance, there is always pressure for a youth movement to be embraced by the U.S. team. Snedeker may be facing that pressure more than any other captain in the Cup's 30-year history, but he isn't succumbing to it, at least not yet.

Those pressures of bringing the 'kids' along to Medinah became as obvious as ever before over the past two weeks with 21-year-old Jackson Koivun winning the 3M Open in just his third start as a professional and 24-year-old Michael Thorbjornsen winning the Rocket Classic for his maiden PGA Tour victory.

Given Koivun's insanely impressive amateur and college career at Auburn and his nearly-immediate win on Tour, much of the golf world went ahead and wrote his name in Sharpie to be named to the Presidents Cup team. Thorbjornsen's name has been penciled in, although he's been sneakily fantastic in his short PGA Tour career.

Snedeker played a practice round with Koivun ahead of this week's Wyndham Championship, and while he praised his game and called him a "generational" player, he made it clear his strategy as captain does not involve bringing on youth for the sake of bringing on youth.

"I don't ever really look at it like we have to change things or do things different. I think the golf dictates who needs to be on the team. I'm not into, 'oh, let's just take a young kid because we need a young kid on the team,'" Snedeker said on Tuesday.

"That doesn't make any sense to me. I think you take the best players who give you the best opportunity of winning. I don't think -- you can't discount what people have done and you can't -- it's really hard to forecast how guys are going to handle those kinds of things. You look at how they've played, what they're capable of, what their ceiling is, what their basement is, what their floor is and kind of go from there."

Snedeker's comments represent the polar opposite viewpoints that leadership in place and golf fans have when looking at the Presidents Cup, but that doesn't mean what he had to say about the situation is wrong.

From a fan's perspective, and it's an understandable one, the Presidents Cup is a warm-up event for the Ryder Cup. With that mindset, why wouldn't Koivun be given a spot on the U.S. team and get match-play reps at the Presidents Cup, when it's assumed he will play his way onto the very short list of players who could represent the red, white, and blue at the 2027 Ryder Cup?

It's a fair question, especially when the U.S. Ryder Cup team has lost nine of the last 12 Ryder Cups dating back to the turn of the century, and needs to (must) try a new approach in 2027.

While Snedeker absolutely wants to see the U.S. team go to Ireland and upset Team Europe in 2027, that is not part of his job description as this year's Presidents Cup captain.

item.title: Republicans move to oust embattled Florida GOP lawmaker in bitter primary fight
item.description: Reps. Cory Mills, Chuck Edwards and Max Miller face misconduct allegations that now threaten GOP control of Congress heading into midterms. Edwards has dropped his campaign.
item.content:encoded:
House GOP divisions are erupting on the midterm campaign trail as Republicans fight an uphill battle to keep control of Congress for the latter half of President Donald Trump's term.

The infighting touched down in Florida on Wednesday, where two House Republicans are endorsing a primary opponent to incumbent Rep. Cory Mills, R-Fla., who is facing multiple investigations into his finances and allegations of domestic abuse, among other claims. Mills has denied any wrongdoing.

Reps. Mike Haridopolos, R-Fla., and Anna Paulina Luna, R-Fla., announced they're backing former local TV anchor Ryan Elijah for Mills' seat and said they "urge our fellow Republicans to join us in supporting him."

"Ryan Elijah is an excellent candidate and will ensure victory for us in Florida 7," Haridopolos told Fox News Digital. The Florida congressman will be in attendance at Mills' debate against Elijah on Wednesday night and plans to sit next to the candidate's wife.

GOP PARTY FISSURES EXPOSED IN BATTLE FOR S.C. SENATE SEAT TO REPLACE GRAHAM: 'I DON'T LIKE HEARING THAT'

Notably, President Donald Trump has endorsed Haridopolos, Luna and Mills for re-election — a fact Mills brought up in his response to Fox News Digital.

"I’m the only candidate in this race endorsed by President Donald Trump. Not once, not twice, but three times. I’m proud to have earned his trust because he knows I’ll continue fighting to advance the America First agenda and deliver results," Mills said. "The fact is, my office has returned more than $107 million to the people of Florida’s 7th District, led Florida in constituent services, built one of the strongest conservative voting records in Congress, and flipped this district from blue to red,and kept it red. My record speaks for itself."

It comes after another GOP source told Fox News Digital that some Florida Republicans were worried about the chances of keeping Mills' seat if he won the primary on Tuesday, Aug. 18.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report downgraded its projection for Republicans from "Solid R" to "Likely R" earlier this year. And with a Cook rating of R+5, Democrats could be within striking distance if Republicans see a tough enough cycle in November.

Mills is under investigation by the House Ethics Committee and the Department of Justice (DOJ), according to a source, though he has consistently insisted that he has not done anything wrong.

WATCH: CORY MILLS BLASTS DOJ PROBE AS ‘POLITICAL OP' AHEAD OF FLORIDA PRIMARY

The Republican military veteran dismissed reports of a DOJ investigation as a "desperate lie" by his opponents and said on X late last month, "We are not aware of any DOJ investigation, nor has there been any confirmation of such investigation by DOJ or FBI, and would fully cooperate if there was one."

Fox News Digital reached out to Mills for a response to Haridopolos and Luna's endorsement.

Mills is one of several House Republicans whose allegations of misconduct are posing a headache for the GOP on the campaign trail.

Rep. Chuck Edwards, R-N.C., announced overnight that he would drop his re-election bid after an explosive report detailed sexual harassment accusations by two young female staffers. Edwards has denied those accusations but has admitted to at times making staff feel uncomfortable.

GOP LAWMAKER'S GIFTS, 'EFFUSIVE AFFECTION' TOWARD YOUNG STAFFERS DETAILED IN EXPLOSIVE ETHICS REPORT

And Rep. Max Miller, R-Ohio, has been accused of domestic abuse by his ex-wife and former father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, and is facing pressure from congressional Republicans to drop out of his race as well. One House GOP source called the situation a "f---ing trainwreck" in comments to Fox News Digital.

Miller has denied any wrongdoing and asked the House Ethics Committee to initiate an investigation in order to clear his name. The former Trump aide has resisted calls to exit the race, insisting he will win in November and that the public accusations from his ex-wife are a bid to derail his political career.

All three House seats are on the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) target list, meaning Democrats are pouring money and resources into those races.

One House Republican, who was granted anonymity to speak freely, told Fox News Digital that all three should drop out of their races, stating, "We must lead by example."

item.title: Political newcomer seeks to unseat twin of Trump impeachment foe in swing Virginia district
item.description: Three GOP political newcomers battled it out in Virginia 7th Congressional District to challenge Rep. Eugene Vindman, twin brother of Trump impeachment witness Alexander Vindman.
item.content:encoded:
Douglas Ollivant decisively beat two fellow political newcomers in the Republican primary contest to take on incumbent Rep. Eugene Vindman, D-Va., in November.

Vindman, whose twin brother is a high-profile foe of President Donald Trump, currently represents Virginia's 7th Congressional district, a seat previously held by the state's Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger.

The Republican primary race between Ollivant, Rick Smithers and Philip Harding was unique in that none of the candidates had held elected office before, though two have government experience. The lack of reliable polling made it difficult to foretell who would emerge triumphant — but Ollivant ran away with victory, earning 56.6% of the vote compared to Harding's 30.7% and Smithers' 12.8%.

Ollivant is a retired Army officer who served as the National Security Council director for Iraq during the George W. Bush administration. He worked as a national security analyst and consultant after that.

Smithers is a pastor and construction business owner who branded himself as the biggest outsider in the race.

Harding is a businessman with a bachelor's degree from Harvard University. He also earned his graduate degree from the Harvard Kennedy School of Government.

All three candidates have generally aligned themselves with Donald Trump, though the president did not endorse anyone in the race.

Virginia's 7th Congressional District, located in the northeastern part of the state and encompassing Culpeper and Fredericksburg east into Stafford, Spotsylvania, Caroline and parts of Prince William County, is considered a true swing state.

Alexander is an ardent defender of Ukraine, and became a central figure of the impeachment attempt, claiming that in a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump attempted to make military aid for the embattled European nation contingent on an investigation into the Biden family's involvement in Ukrainian business activities.

item.title: Secret FBI probe cast Trump as possible Russian asset after Comey firing, memos show
item.description: Declassified FBI memos reveal the bureau opened a counterintelligence probe codenamed "Oxferd Comma" after Trump fired James Comey in 2017.
item.content:encoded:
The White House released newly declassified FBI memos showing that the bureau opened a 2017 counterintelligence investigation into whether President Donald Trump’s firing of James Comey was connected to Russia.

The investigation, codenamed "Oxferd Comma," opened after Trump fired FBI Director James Comey in May 2017, according to the White House's release. It is unclear as to why the word "Oxford" was seemingly misspelled.

The probe was launched due to national security concerns about whether Trump himself was a Russian asset, the documents allege.

Investigators sought to determine whether Trump was "directed by, controlled by, and/or coordinated activities with, the Russian Federation in a manner constituting a threat to the national security of the United States and/or a violation of federal criminal statutes," according an FBI memo on May 16, 2017, jump-starting the investigation.

"In addition, this investigation will also seek to determine whether President Trump and others yet to be named obstructed and/or conspiracy to obstruct any associated FBI investigation," the same memo added.

Comey was appointed by then-President Barack Obama, serving as FBI Director from 2013 to 2017.

He oversaw the launch of the "Crossfire Hurricane" investigation in July 2016 after receiving information that Trump campaign adviser George Papadopoulos had suggested Russia possessed damaging information about Hillary Clinton.

SUPREME COURT DECLINES TO REVIVE CARTER PAGE LAWSUIT OVER FBI SURVEILLANCE TIED TO TRUMP-RUSSIA PROBE

Comey also ran an investigation into Clinton about the use of her private email servers and sent a letter to Congress days before the 2016 election saying the FBI had discovered emails that "appear to be pertinent." 

Trump fired Comey after taking office, with the administration initially citing his handling of the Clinton email investigation as reason for losing his job.

COMEY LEARNS FATE OF BID TO DELAY TRIAL OVER ‘86 47’ SEASHELL POST AT CENTER OF TRUMP THREAT CASE

A week after Comey’s firing, Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein appointed Robert Mueller as Special Counsel to take over and broaden the existing FBI "Crossfire Hurricane" investigation. 

Mueller found in April 2019 that the Russian government sought to influence the election through a social media disinformation campaign and by hacking and releasing Democratic Party emails. His report stated that the investigation did not establish that members of the Trump campaign conspired or coordinated with the Russian government.

After Mueller's probe was set to be finalized, memos on the "Oxferd Comma" investigation were closed on April 9, 2019.

Subsequently, Attorney General William Barr appointed John Durham to review how the FBI had initiated the Russia investigation, which in 2023 concluded that the Bureau lacked sufficient factual basis to open the full Crossfire Hurricane investigation and exhibited bias by departing from its usual standards.

New documents on a declassified annex to Durham's final report show that officials had concerns rgarding Clinton’s campaign plan to smear then-candidate Trump by connecting him to Russia.

"Raising the theme of "Putin's support for Trump" to the level of the Olympics scandal would divert the constituents' attention from the investigation of Clinton's compromised electronic correspondence," reads the annex.

Included in the annex is a 2016 letter from Leonard Benardo, who worked for the Soros-founded philanthropic network Open Society Foundations and had business in Moscow in the 1980s.

"Julie says it will be a long-term affair to demonize Putin and Trump. Now it is good for a post-convention bounce. Later the FBI will put more oil into the fire," wrote Benardo. 

The ‘Julie’ that Benardo references appears to be Clinton foreign policy advisor Julianne Smith, according to the report appendix.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for additional comment on Wednesday. 

This is a breaking news story and will be updated.

item.title: Shaquille O'Neal talks LeBron James' Lakers legacy, why his new 76ers might be extremely 'dangerous'
item.description: Shaquille O'Neal ranks LeBron James in the Lakers hierarchy and raises concerns about the Philadelphia 76ers' ball-sharing with Joel Embiid.
item.content:encoded:
In an unprecedented 24th season in the NBA, LeBron James will try to make even more history with his new fourth team.

James signed a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers late last month, joining a team with newly acquired Jaylen Brown, one-time MVP Joel Embiid and scoring machine Tyrese Maxey to make them a championship contender in the Eastern Conference.

No player has ever won an NBA title with four separate teams (James is one of four players to win with three, along with John Salley, Robert Horry and Danny Green), but before James tries to bring one to Philly for the first time since 1983, his Los Angeles Lakers legacy is already a hot topic.

"He definitely won a championship there and was a big game player, so he’s in the building," O'Neal told Fox News Digital in a recent interview.

But he stopped short of putting him in the "top floor."

"Top floor belongs to Magic (Johnson), Kobe (Bryant), and Kareem (Abdul-Jabbar). I’m going to put Kareem," O'Neal continued. "The second floor is me and those other guys.

"Even though I’m 54, when I get home by myself and I’m watching a movie, I like to take it back to when I was age nine or 10 where mom and dad were sleeping. I’d go downstairs, get a nice bowl of cereal, and I'd have to wash the bowl before they got up so nobody knew I had my bowl of cereal... Teaming up with General Mills was a perfect fit because I’ve been eating these cereals forever."

The one thing about James' move to the City of Brotherly Love, however, is that there is, in fact, just one basketball.

item.title: Perez Hilton under involuntary psych hold after apparent self-harm livestream: source
item.description: Miami-Dade deputies responded to Perez Hilton's home after receiving multiple reports about an apparent self-harm incident during a TikTok livestream.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Law enforcement was called to Perez Hilton's Miami residence after the celebrity blogger appeared to be harming himself during a TikTok livestream on Tuesday evening.

"The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office received multiple calls regarding an individual who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media," a spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Deputies quickly located the individual’s residence, where they spoke with family members on scene, and confirmed he was alone inside."

"In many incidents involving a person experiencing a mental health crisis or actively harming themselves, deputies prioritize de-escalation by creating time, distance, and opportunities for communication. Unless there is an immediate threat to others, slowing the situation and utilizing crisis intervention techniques can reduce the likelihood of a suicide-by-cop encounter and minimize the risk of injury to the individual, deputies, and the public."

CELEBRITY BLOGGER PEREZ HILTON SAYS HE FOUND GOD AMID MEDICAL SCARE IN EMOTIONAL CONFESSION

"At this time, deputies have tactically disengaged while continuing to monitor the situation and providing the needed support to his family," the statement concludes. 

The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital that the individual had been "safely recovered and transported by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue to a local hospital, where he is receiving medical attention."

"The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office Crisis Response Unit and Licensed Mental Health Professionals are also on scene providing support and resources to the individual’s family."

A source close to the situation tells Fox News Digital that Hilton was placed under a psychiatric hold under the Baker Act and "had wounds and cuts all over the place." 

"He’s alive," the source added. "He has superficial cuts all over the body."

The Florida Baker Act is a state law that gives law enforcement officers, judges and certain mental health professionals the authority to place an individual into an involuntary mental health evaluation when specific legal criteria are met. 

Under the Baker Act, an individual can be transported to a designated receiving facility for an emergency psychiatric evaluation that generally lasts up to 72 hours.

On Wednesday, Hilton's family and team released a statement regarding his ongoing hospitalization. 

"Many of you have reached out with concern for Perez, and we are incredibly grateful for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers," the statement read. "We can confirm that Perez is receiving medical care, and our family’s focus right now is on his well-being. We kindly ask that you respect Perez’s privacy, as well as the privacy of his family, during this difficult time."

"If and when we are able to share any updates, we will do so with everyone as soon as we can," the statement concluded. "Thank you for your compassion, understanding, and continued support."

A representative for Hilton did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. 

The content creator recently moved to Miami with his mother, 73, and his three young children.

Hilton, born Mario Armando Lavandeira Jr., rose to fame in the mid-2000s after launching his celebrity gossip website in 2004. The Miami native quickly became one of the internet's most influential entertainment voices, known for breaking celebrity news and his unfiltered commentary.

The media personality has frequently shared how parenthood has reshaped his priorities, often offering followers a glimpse into family life on social media.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Earlier this year, Hilton revealed he had been hospitalized for 21 days after a severe case of sepsis stemming from complications related to the flu. The celebrity blogger said he developed an ulcer and stomach perforation after taking medication on an empty stomach, ultimately requiring emergency surgery and weeks of treatment.

In a candid video he shared at the time, he said God had "presented himself to me" during the ordeal and changed him through the experience.

"God presented himself to me and then did something. Something I can only call miraculous... it was real, and this has been life-changing," he said.

In a follow-up video, the entertainment columnist tearfully apologized for past mistakes and said he had begun reading the Bible again.

"I’ve been crying, but happy tears. Happy tears. Because this is just, this is just so crazy. I’ve been reading the Bible, and so much of what is said here I had already been thinking of. It’s just overwhelming in the best, most beautiful way," he said while holding up a Bible to the camera.

"I made a lot of mistakes in my past. We all have. Nobody's perfect," he said. "But my mistakes are very public. The internet is forever. Receipts are forever. I carry with me deep shame and regret. I'm sorry. I will continue to apologize. I have also reached out to make amends. I've apologized publicly and privately to dozens of people."

"Because I was so selfish, because I didn't care who I hurt. I just cared about the views, the attention, the money — people hated me," he continued. "Some people enjoyed it, but it felt like most people hated me. And last week, since I've been home, I haven't been getting as much hate, and I've been getting love and prayers."

Hilton added, "And I know that some people are fed up with me talking about God. You don’t have to watch these videos. You don’t have to watch. I love God. My experience was real. My testimony is important."

"What matters is today. How I behave today, how I behave tomorrow," he continued. "And not only did God save me in so many ways, but God gave me a new lease on life and a new opportunity to truly be better and do better."

item.title: Fake party invitation scam can hijack your computer
item.description: Fake party invitations trick victims into downloading malware that gives criminals remote access to computers and spreads through contact lists.
item.content:encoded:
You sit down at your computer to clear out your inbox. Then you spot a party invitation from someone you recognize. Maybe it appears to come from a friend. Perhaps the sender belongs to a group you know. Either way, the familiar name makes the message feel safe enough to open.

Inside, everything looks cheerful. There is an envelope graphic, a friendly note and what appears to be an invitation for a wedding or retirement party. However, you cannot see the event details yet. The message tells you to save the invitation or install something to join the guest list.

That request should stop you cold. A legitimate party invitation should not require you to install software before you can see when or where the event takes place. That small download could give a criminal remote access to your computer. Here’s how this fake invitation scam works and what you can do before one click puts your computer and contacts at risk.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?", has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE SHINYHUNTERS SEXTORTION EMAIL USES CARNIVAL BREACH DATA

The scam begins with trust. An invitation appears to come from someone whose name you recognize, so you become less suspicious. Criminals may copy the look of a legitimate invitation platform. They can add a colorful envelope, an exclusive-sounding message and a button that promises to reveal the details.

The email has one main purpose: getting you to click. Once you press the invitation, the message sends you to a separate website. That page says a friend sent you something and asks you to download a file to view it.

The request may seem simple. Still, party invitations normally open inside a website or app. They do not need to install a program on your computer.

The landing page may contain a large "Download invitation" button. It may also display a familiar company name inside the web address. However, seeing a trusted brand somewhere in a link proves very little. Criminals can place that name inside a much longer address or add extra letters that make the domain look authentic at a glance.

You need to identify the real domain instead of focusing on the first familiar word you see. The page may also create confusion. It could claim that your invitation is already downloading while another message asks you to click if the download fails. Some versions even include a testimonial from a supposed guest who says opening the invitation was easy.

A review on a private party invitation page should feel strange. Those details are designed to quiet your doubts and push you toward the download button. For more visual breakdowns of scams like this, check out The CyberGuy Report podcast at CyberGuy.com.

In the example we describe, the website directs you to open the file on a Windows computer. That device-specific request is another major warning sign. Why would a party invitation care which device you use? The malicious file may contain a remote access tool. Businesses use legitimate versions of this software to troubleshoot computers from another location.

Criminals can abuse similar tools to control your system without permission. Once you install the file, an attacker may be able to search your computer or access saved information. The exact damage depends on the program and the permissions it receives. Your email account can become an especially valuable target. It contains personal conversations along with a contact list filled with people who trust you.

The criminals can then send the same fake invitation to your friends and relatives. Those people may open it because the message appears to come from your real account. As a result, one compromised computer can start a chain reaction.

People receive a steady stream of spam, fake alerts and impersonation attempts. Criminals can also use AI tools to create cleaner writing and more realistic designs. That makes the familiar sender name even more powerful.

You may be cautious around a message from a stranger. Yet you might act quickly when the invitation appears to come from someone you know. The scam succeeds when familiarity replaces verification. Email providers and technology companies continue to improve their filters. Even so, dangerous messages still reach real inboxes. That leaves you making the final decision about whether a link deserves your trust.

HOTEL WI-FI PHISHING ATTACK TARGETS MICROSOFT LOGINS

A few precautions can help you recognize a malicious invitation before it compromises your computer or accounts.

Use strong antivirus software and keep it actively running in the background on your devices. Real-time protection can warn you about a dangerous link or block a malicious download before it reaches your computer.

If you clicked the invitation or downloaded a suspicious file, delete the file without opening it and run a full security scan. A scan can help identify unwanted software that may have reached your computer. Keep your operating system, browser and security software updated as well. Updates often close weaknesses that criminals try to exploit. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com

Stop immediately if an invitation tells you to download or install a program before you can see the event. Real invitation services normally show the details in your browser or inside their official app. You should not need a separate installer. Delete the message instead of trying to see what happens next.

On a computer, place your cursor over a link without pressing it. Your browser or email program should reveal the destination address. Read the entire address carefully. Watch for misspellings, unexpected words or extra letters added around a legitimate company name. A familiar logo does not confirm that the link belongs to the real company.

Avoid using the link inside the email when you have doubts. Instead, type the invitation service's web address into your browser or open its official app. Sign in and look for the invitation there. If it does not appear in your account, the email may be fake.

Reach out through a separate text message or phone call if an invitation feels unusual. Do not reply directly to the suspicious email. A criminal may control the sender's account or may have forged the address. Ask whether the person actually sent the invitation and whether it requires a download.

FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK

Your risk is generally lower if you visited the page but did not run anything. Close the browser tab without pressing the download button. If the file has already downloaded, leave it closed and delete it. Opening the file gives the malicious program a chance to run. Never open it simply to find out what it contains.

Use your email provider's Report phishing option before deleting the invitation. Reporting the message can help the provider block similar emails and warn other recipients. You can also block the sender if you do not recognize the address.

A data removal service can help remove your details from many public data broker databases. This may make it harder for scammers to find personal information they can use to make a message feel convincing. However, no service can remove every record. It also cannot prevent a criminal from reaching you through a compromised friend's contact list. Still, reducing your public exposure can give scammers less material to work with. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) for your email account. This adds another barrier if criminals steal or guess your password. Never approve an unexpected login request. Also, do not share a security code with anyone who contacts you.

If you typed your email address, password or security code into the fake page, use a clean device to change that password immediately. Change it anywhere else you reused it. Then review the account for unfamiliar activity, new recovery information or settings you did not change. Use a password manager to create and store a strong, unique password for every account so one stolen login cannot unlock several services.

Disconnect the computer from the internet if you ran the installer or noticed unexpected remote activity. Next, run a full security scan. You may also need help from a trusted computer professional to confirm that the remote access software is gone. Use a different, clean device to change important passwords. Start with your email account because criminals may use it to reset passwords for other services. Also, review your email account for unfamiliar forwarding rules or active login sessions. Warn your contacts if suspicious messages may have gone out under your name.

A party invitation should give you information, not demand access to your computer. Delete the message if it asks you to install anything before revealing the event. Check the full destination of every link. Then contact the supposed sender separately when something feels unusual. If you downloaded a file but did not open it, delete it and run a security scan. If you ran the file, disconnect the computer and secure your accounts from a clean device. Most importantly, pay attention to that moment when something feels off. A few seconds of doubt can stop a criminal from getting inside your computer. Want to see more? Check out The CyberGuy Report podcast.
